from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = ["We measure distance by simple magnitude.", "Standard convergence means points get closer.", "A hiker approaches a signpost steadily."]
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisite: The Usual Notion of Convergence", lecture_lines)
        
        # Elements
        line = NumberLine(x_range=[0, 2, 0.5], length=5)
        hiker = Dot(color=YELLOW)
        signpost = Dot(color=BLUE)
        
        self.place_at_grid(line, "C2")
        self.place_at_grid(hiker, "C2")
        self.place_at_grid(signpost, "C4")
        
        # Labels
        label_h = Text("Hiker", font_size=16).next_to(hiker, DOWN)
        label_s = Text("Limit", font_size=16).next_to(signpost, DOWN)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))
        self.play(Create(line), FadeIn(hiker), FadeIn(signpost), FadeIn(label_h), FadeIn(label_s))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FF00FF"))
        # Visualize convergence
        target = self.grid["C4"]
        self.play(hiker.animate.move_to(target), run_time=2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#00FFFF"))
        self.play(Indicate(signpost))
        self.wait(1)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Introducing the 2-adic Metric", [
            "The 2-adic metric uses divisibility by two.", 
            "High powers of two make numbers small.", 
            "Binary digits determine 2-adic proximity."
        ])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        norm_text = MathTex(r"|x|_2 = 2^{-v_2(x)}", color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(norm_text, "B2", scale_factor=1.2)
        self.play(Write(norm_text))
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        val_text = MathTex(r"v_2(8) = v_2(2^3) = 3", color="#FFFF00")
        self.place_at_grid(val_text, "C2", scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(Write(val_text))
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FFFF00"))
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        dist_text = MathTex(r"d_2(x, y) = |x - y|_2", color="#FF00FF")
        self.place_at_grid(dist_text, "D2", scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(Write(dist_text))
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FF00FF"))

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Summing powers of two diverges normally.",
            "In 2-adic space, it actually converges.",
            "Increasing powers of two shrink toward negative one.",
            "This defies standard intuition about infinite series.",
            "Different metrics reveal hidden convergence structures."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Paradoxical Convergence", lecture_lines)
        
        # Animations
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        r_line = Line(start=self.grid["B1"], end=self.grid["B6"], color=RED)
        dot_r = Dot(color=RED).move_to(self.grid["B1"])
        label_r = Text("Real Space (Diverges)", font_size=16, color=RED).next_to(r_line, UP)
        self.add(r_line, dot_r, label_r)
        
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(RED))
        self.play(dot_r.animate.move_to(self.grid["B6"]), run_time=2)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        q2_line = Line(start=self.grid["E1"], end=self.grid["E6"], color=GREEN)
        dot_q2 = Dot(color=GREEN).move_to(self.grid["E6"])
        label_q2 = Text("2-adic Space (Converges)", font_size=16, color=GREEN).next_to(q2_line, DOWN)
        self.add(q2_line, dot_q2, label_q2)
        
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(GREEN))
        self.play(dot_q2.animate.move_to(self.grid["E1"]), run_time=2)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        target_point = Dot(color=YELLOW).move_to(self.grid["E1"])
        self.add(target_point)
        self.play(Indicate(target_point))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(LIGHT_GRAY))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(BLUE))

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Visualizing the 2-adic Ultrametric Property", [
            "Ultrametric spaces follow a stronger rule.",
            "Points land in nested bucket structures.",
            "Distance doesn't add up like paths."
        ])
        
        # --- Animation for Lecture Line 1 ---
        # Show three points forming a triangle.
        p1 = Dot(color=WHITE)
        p2 = Dot(color=WHITE)
        p3 = Dot(color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(p1, 'B2')
        self.place_at_grid(p2, 'D2')
        self.place_at_grid(p3, 'D5')
        triangle = Polygon(p1.get_center(), p2.get_center(), p3.get_center(), color=WHITE)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(triangle, p1, p2, p3))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFFFF")

        # --- Animation for Lecture Line 2 ---
        # Visualize the strong triangle inequality.
        # Nested buckets (circles)
        c1 = Circle(radius=0.5, color="#00FF00")
        c2 = Circle(radius=1.0, color="#00FF00")
        self.place_at_grid(c1, 'D3')
        self.place_at_grid(c2, 'D3')
        
        self.play(FadeIn(c1, c2))
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#00FF00")

        # --- Animation for Lecture Line 3 ---
        # Demonstrate the ultrametric property visually.
        # "Bouncing ball" path
        ball = Dot(color="#FFFF00", radius=0.15)
        self.place_at_grid(ball, 'B2')
        path = VMobject(color="#FFFF00")
        path.set_points_smoothly([self.grid['B2'], self.grid['D5'], self.grid['B6']])
        
        self.play(MoveAlongPath(ball, path), run_time=2)
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FFFF00")
        self.wait(1)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Summary and Synthesis", [
            "Real numbers focus on total magnitude.",
            "2-adic numbers focus on divisibility structure.",
            "Perspective changes what convergence means."
        ])
        
        # --- Visual Elements ---
        # Real/Magnitude side
        real_label = Text("Real Magnitude", color=YELLOW).scale(0.6)
        self.place_at_grid(real_label, 'B2')
        
        # 2-adic/Divisibility side
        padic_label = Text("2-adic Divisibility", color=BLUE).scale(0.6)
        self.place_at_grid(padic_label, 'B5')

        # --- Animations ---
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))
        circle = Circle(radius=0.5, color=YELLOW).set_stroke(width=4)
        self.place_at_grid(circle, 'D2')
        self.play(Create(circle))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#00FFFF"))
        square = Square(side_length=1, color=BLUE).set_stroke(width=4)
        self.place_at_grid(square, 'D5')
        self.play(Create(square))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FF00FF"))
        path = VGroup(
            Line(self.grid['D2'], self.grid['D5'], color=WHITE),
            Dot(self.grid['D2']),
            Dot(self.grid['D5'])
        )
        self.play(Create(path))
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: Exploring the 2-adic Metric: Where Infinities Behave Differently
outline.target_audience: Undergraduate mathematics students or advanced high school students

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Usual Notion of Convergence
sections.content: Briefly revisit the Euclidean metric (standard distance). Explain that in the real number line, a sum converges if the 'tail' of the sequence gets arbitrarily close to zero in magnitude. Visualize this as a point moving closer and closer to a destination on a line.
sections.example: Visualizing the geometric series 1/2 + 1/4 + 1/8... as a hiker approaching a signpost 1 mile away.

sections.title: Introducing the 2-adic Metric
sections.content: Define the 2-adic valuation: a number is 'small' if it is divisible by high powers of 2. Introduce the 2-adic distance: |x - y|_2 = 2^(-v_2(x-y)). Explain that higher powers of 2 make points 'closer'.
sections.example: A digital robot that considers two numbers 'close' if their binary representations share many common digits starting from the right (the least significant bit).

sections.title: Paradoxical Convergence
sections.content: Demonstrate the core concept: the infinite sum 1 + 2 + 4 + 8 + ... converges in the 2-adic metric. Contrast this with the real number line, where this sum clearly diverges to infinity.
sections.example: An animation showing 2^n getting smaller in 2-adic space, collapsing toward -1, while in standard space it shoots off to the edge of the screen.

sections.title: Visualizing the 2-adic Ultrametric Property
sections.content: Introduce the Strong Triangle Inequality: |x + y|_2 ≤ max(|x|_2, |y|_2). This defines a 'non-Archimedean' space. Visualize this as a fractal-like tree structure (the Cantor set or p-adic tree) where every point is either identical or completely separate.
sections.example: A 'bouncing ball' analogy where the ball can only jump to positions that are powers of 2, landing in 'nested buckets' rather than sliding along a flat floor.

sections.title: Summary and Synthesis
sections.content: Synthesize the two worlds: Real numbers measure size by 'magnitude', while p-adic numbers measure size by 'divisibility'. Highlight how this shifts our understanding of what it means for an infinite series to 'settle down'.
sections.example: A split-screen comparison: A mountain climber (Real) vs. a code-breaker (2-adic) analyzing the same sequence of numbers.
